description: Raw responses from the NIST Chemistry WebBook fluid property service (NIST Standard Reference Database 69, 'Thermophysical Properties of Fluid Systems'), saved byte for byte. The water entry in src/emergent_matter_materials/catalog/liquids.py is copied from these files, and tests/test_water_nist_webbook.py checks every catalogued number against them.
retrieved_note: Retrieval time is the HTTP Date header of the responses.

units.Cp (J/g*K): J/(g*K); the catalog stores J/(kg*K), multiplied by 1000

formulations.Equation of state (density, Cp): Wagner, W.; Pruss, A., The IAPWS Formulation 1995 for the Thermodynamic Properties of Ordinary Water Substance for General and Scientific Use, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data, 2002, 31, 2, 387-535, https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1461829. IAPWS R6-95, Revised Release on the IAPWS Formulation 1995, 2016.
formulations.Viscosity: Huber, M.L. et al., New International Formulation for the Viscosity of H2O, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data, 2009, 38, 2, 101-125, https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3088050. IAPWS Release on the IAPWS Formulation 2008 for the Viscosity of Ordinary Water Substance.
formulations.Thermal conductivity: Huber, M.L. et al., New International Formulation for the Thermal Conductivity of H2O, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data, 2012, 41, 3, 033102, https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4738955. IAPWS Release on the IAPWS Formulation 2011 for the Thermal Conductivity of Ordinary Water Substance.

uncertainty_as_stated_by_nist.Density: 0.0001% at 1 atm in the liquid phase
uncertainty_as_stated_by_nist.Viscosity: Not stated on the results page; NIST refers to the IAPWS release or the cited publication
uncertainty_as_stated_by_nist.Thermal conductivity: Not stated on the results page; NIST refers to the IAPWS release or the cited publication

water_isobar_0.101325MPa_0C_to_100C.tsv.used_for: The 0.01 C row only. NIST's isobar starts at the triple point (0.01 C), so a 0 C start returns 0.01 C and then a grid offset by 0.01 C.

water_isobar_0.101325MPa_5C_to_100C.tsv.used_for: Every liquid row, 5 C to 99.9743 C (saturated liquid at the normal boiling point). The vapor rows after it are not used.
